title: Pride and Prejudice
subjects: British and Irish fiction (fictional works by one author)
synopsis: Elizabeth Bennet, a witty and independent young woman in early nineteenth-century England, navigates family pressure, class expectations and first impressions. When she meets the proud Mr. Darcy, mutual misunderstanding turns their relationship into a sharp contest of wit, pride and prejudice.

title: Jane Eyre
synopsis: Orphaned and mistreated as a child, Jane grows into a determined and principled governess. Her new post at Thornfield Hall draws her toward its brooding master, Mr. Rochester, and toward secrets hidden within the house. A story of moral independence and hard-won love.

title: Wuthering Heights
subjects: British and irish fiction (fictional works by one author)
synopsis: On the bleak Yorkshire moors, a tangled story of passion, class and revenge unfolds across two generations. A visitor named Lockwood rents a remote farmhouse and learns about the troubled families of the Heights and the Grange from the housekeeper, Nelly Dean. Obsessive love becomes a destructive force.

title: Frankenstein
subtitle: ou O Prometeu Moderno
synopsis: Young scientist Victor Frankenstein creates a living being through forbidden experiments, then recoils from what he has made. Told through letters and nested narratives, the novel asks what responsibility a creator owes to his creation, and how ambition and isolation can corrupt good intentions.

title: Dracula
synopsis: Solicitor Jonathan Harker travels to a remote Transylvanian castle to finish a property sale for an aristocratic client. The trip becomes a gothic nightmare, and the story unfolds through letters, diaries and clippings as a small group races to understand an ancient menace arriving from the East.

title: Moby-Dick
synopsis: Ishmael signs on to a whaling voyage aboard the Pequod, under the captain, Ahab. Narrated with encyclopedic digressions on whales and the sea trade, the novel follows an obsessive quest against a great white whale, exploring faith, fate and the limits of human control over nature.

title: The Great Gatsby
subjects: American fiction (fictional works by one author)
synopsis: Nick Carraway, a young bond salesman, moves to Long Island in the summer of 1922 and lives beside the mysterious, lavish Jay Gatsby. Through Nick's eyes we see glittering parties, a yearning for a lost romance and the careless wealth of the rich, a portrait of the American Dream.

title: To Kill a Mockingbird
synopsis: In a small Depression-era Alabama town, six-year-old Scout Finch watches her lawyer father defend a Black man wrongly accused of assaulting a white woman. Seen through a child's eyes, the novel explores moral courage, racial injustice and the loss of innocence in a community obsessed with appearances.

subjects: British and irish fiction (fictional works by one author)
synopsis: In a totalitarian superstate where the Party watches every move, Winston Smith rewrites historical records at the Ministry of Truth to match official lies. Secretly doubting the regime, he begins a forbidden diary and an illicit relationship, a chilling study of surveillance, propaganda and the fragility of independent thought.

title: Brave New World
subjects: Moral and ethical aspects of Science
synopsis: In a future World State engineered for stability, people are bred and conditioned into fixed social castes and kept content with pleasure, entertainment and a drug called soma. Several characters begin to question this comfortable order, and the novel examines technology, consumerism and the meaning of freedom.

title: The Catcher in the Rye
synopsis: Sixteen-year-old Holden Caulfield recounts a few turbulent days after being expelled from his prep school and wanders New York City alone. Meeting old acquaintances and strangers, he reflects with bitter humor on phoniness, grief and the adult world he is about to enter.

title: Crime and Punishment
synopsis: In St. Petersburg, an impoverished former student named Raskolnikov commits a murder he believes he can justify through a theory of extraordinary people. Tormented by guilt and paranoia, he is drawn into a psychological duel with a shrewd investigator, a tale of conscience, poverty and redemption.

title: Anna Karenina
synopsis: In imperial Russia, the glamorous Anna enters a passionate affair with a dashing officer, upending her marriage and her reputation in aristocratic society. Alongside her story runs that of Konstantin Levin, a landowner searching for meaning in farming and faith, in a sweeping portrait of love and social hypocrisy.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
subjects: Continental european fiction (fictional works by one author)
synopsis: The wealthy and debauched Fyodor Karamazov is found murdered in his provincial town, and each of his three sons has a reason to wish him dead. Dostoevsky's final novel probes faith, free will, doubt and morality through long philosophical debates, family rivalries and the question of who bears responsibility for a crime.

title: The Count of Monte Cristo
synopsis: Edmond Dantes, a young sailor on the verge of becoming a captain, is falsely accused of treason and imprisoned without trial. After years of captivity he escapes with a hidden fortune and reinvents himself as a mysterious count, carefully orchestrating revenge on those who betrayed him.

title: Les Misérables
subjects: Continental european fiction (fictional works by one author)
synopsis: Jean Valjean, a former convict marked by his past, tries to build a new life of virtue in post-revolutionary France. Relentlessly hunted by the police inspector Javert, he takes responsibility for a young girl named Cosette. Victor Hugo's sweeping novel follows the poor and rebellious across decades of upheaval.

title: A Tale of Two Cities
subjects: British and irish fiction (fictional works by one author)
synopsis: Set against the French Revolution and London of the 1780s, this novel follows a disillusioned English lawyer and a French émigré who look strikingly alike. Their intertwined lives cross the boundaries of class, love and sacrifice as the violence of revolution spreads, building toward an act of redemption.

title: The Picture of Dorian Gray
subjects: British and irish fiction (fictional works by one author)
synopsis: A strikingly beautiful young man in Victorian London wishes that his portrait would age while he stays youthful. As he indulges in pleasure and vice without visible consequence, the painting records every corruption. Oscar Wilde's witty, dark novel meditates on vanity, hedonism and the cost of a life lived for appearances.

title: Strange Case of Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde
synopsis: The lawyer Gabriel Utterson investigates strange events linking his old friend Dr. Henry Jekyll to a brutal figure named Edward Hyde. Told through letters and documents, Robert Louis Stevenson's short novel explores the duality of human nature, respectability and hidden desire.

title: Treasure Island
synopsis: Young Jim Hawkins finds a treasure map in an old sea chest at a seaside inn. He soon sails for the island with a crew that includes the charming but dangerous one-legged cook, Long John Silver. A classic adventure of pirates, mutiny and buried gold, told with vivid storytelling.

title: The Adventures of Sherlock Holmes
synopsis: Twelve short stories feature the London detective Sherlock Holmes and his loyal companion, Dr. John Watson. Holmes's sharp observation and deductive reasoning solve cases involving stolen jewels, missing persons and strange ciphers. Arthur Conan Doyle's collection helped define the modern detective story.

title: The Hound of the Baskervilles
subjects: British and irish fiction (fictional works by one author)
synopsis: A legendary curse hangs over the Baskerville family of Dartmoor, and a spectral hound is said to haunt the moors. When the heir, Sir Henry, arrives from abroad, Sherlock Holmes is called in to investigate. Set in mist-covered moorland, the novel blends Gothic atmosphere with methodical detection.

title: Alice's Adventures in Wonderland
subjects: British and irish fiction (fictional works by one author)
synopsis: Bored on a summer afternoon, Alice follows a talking White Rabbit down a hole into a topsy-turvy world. She meets peculiar creatures, changes size unexpectedly, attends a mad tea party and encounters a queen who loves to order executions. Lewis Carroll's playful fantasy delights in logic games and nonsense.

title: Peter Pan
synopsis: Wendy, John and Michael Darling are whisked from their London nursery by a boy who refuses to grow up. Together they fly to Neverland, where they meet pirates, mermaids and lost boys. J.M. Barrie's story explores childhood, imagination and the bittersweet passage into adulthood.

title: The Wind in the Willows
publisher: Hang kong gong ye chu ban she
synopsis: Mole, Rat, Badger and the boastful Toad share a riverbank world of picnics, boats and cozy homes in the English countryside. Kenneth Grahame's gentle classic follows their friendships and small adventures, celebrating home, nature and loyalty, with a memorable spree involving Toad's motorcars.

title: The Secret Garden
synopsis: After her parents die in India, the sour, spoiled orphan Mary Lennox is sent to a gloomy Yorkshire manor. She discovers a hidden, locked garden and, with help from a local boy and a sickly cousin, begins to bring it back to life. Frances Hodgson Burnett's novel is about healing, growth and friendship.

title: Little Women
synopsis: The four March sisters, Meg, Jo, Beth and Amy, navigate childhood, ambition and romance during the American Civil War while their father serves as a chaplain far from home. Louisa May Alcott's warm, witty novel celebrates family loyalty, creative aspiration and the joys and sorrows of growing up.

title: The Time Machine
subjects: English literature, history and criticism, 19th century
synopsis: A Victorian inventor builds a machine that carries him far into the future, to a world divided between gentle, childlike Eloi and brutish Morlocks. H.G. Wells uses this journey to speculate about class, evolution and the fate of humanity, and the short novel helped define the time-travel story.

title: The War of the Worlds
synopsis: Mysterious cylinders land near London, and towering Martian war machines begin to devastate the countryside. Told by an unnamed narrator who witnesses the invasion and its chaos, H.G. Wells's classic early alien-invasion tale comments on imperial arrogance and human vulnerability.

title: The Old Man and the Sea
synopsis: An aging Cuban fisherman, Santiago, has gone eighty-four days without catching a fish. Venturing far into the Gulf Stream, he hooks a giant marlin and begins a grueling battle of endurance and will. Ernest Hemingway's short novel is a spare, profound meditation on pride, solitude and dignity in defeat.

title: To the Lighthouse
synopsis: The Ramsay family and their guests spend a summer at a house on the Scottish island of Skye, and a planned trip to a distant lighthouse is repeatedly postponed. Virginia Woolf's experimental novel moves through shifting perspectives and inner thoughts, exploring memory, art, marriage and the passage of time.

title: Lord of the Flies
subjects: British and irish fiction (fictional works by one author)
synopsis: A group of British boys is stranded on a deserted tropical island after a plane crash, with no adults to guide them. They try to build a society with rules and leadership, but fear, rivalry and savagery soon erode their civilization. William Golding's allegorical novel examines the darker side of human nature.

title: The Grapes of Wrath
synopsis: Tom Joad, newly paroled from prison, returns to his Oklahoma farm to find his family dispossessed by drought and debt. Joining migrants heading west toward California, the Joads face hunger, exploitation and stubborn hope. John Steinbeck's novel is a powerful portrait of the Dust Bowl era and the struggle for dignity.

title: Rebecca
synopsis: A young woman, who remains unnamed, marries the wealthy widower Maxim de Winter and moves to his grand estate, Manderley. There she is haunted by the memory of his first wife, Rebecca, and by the sinister housekeeper, Mrs. Danvers. Daphne du Maurier's gothic novel is a suspenseful study of jealousy and identity.

title: Gone with the Wind
synopsis: In Georgia on the eve of the American Civil War, the headstrong Scarlett O'Hara is determined to win the affections of Ashley Wilkes, who is engaged to another woman. As war destroys the South and its plantation way of life, Scarlett fights to survive and rebuild. Margaret Mitchell's epic novel explores love, loss and resilience.

title: Their Eyes Were Watching God
synopsis: Janie Crawford, a Black woman in early twentieth-century Florida, tells her life story through three marriages and a long search for love and self-fulfillment. Recounting it to her friend Pheoby, Janie reflects on the expectations her community has placed on her. Zora Neale Hurston's vibrant novel is written in rich dialect and lyrical prose.

title: Beloved
synopsis: Sethe, a former enslaved woman living in Ohio after the Civil War, is haunted by memories and by the daughter she lost. When a mysterious young woman arrives, the household confronts the traumas of slavery and the weight of memory. Toni Morrison's Pulitzer Prize-winning novel is a haunting story of love and survival.

title: Fahrenheit 451
synopsis: In a future America where books are banned and burned, fireman Guy Montag enforces the law until a chance encounter with a curious young neighbor makes him question everything. Ray Bradbury's novel is a lyrical warning about censorship, mass entertainment and the power of ideas.

title: Catch-22
synopsis: Captain John Yossarian, a bombardier in World War II, is desperate to escape flying more missions over Italy. Military bureaucracy offers a maddening loophole called Catch-22, and his attempts to outwit it lead to absurd, darkly comic episodes. Joseph Heller's satire explores war, logic and institutional madness.

title: Lolita
synopsis: Humbert Humbert, a cultured European émigré, narrates his obsession with a young girl named Dolores in postwar America. Vladimir Nabokov's brilliant, unreliable narrator offers ornate, self-justifying prose that gradually reveals the horror of his actions, making the novel a provocative study of desire and self-deception.

title: Don Quixote
synopsis: Alonso Quixano, an aging Spanish gentleman, reads so many chivalric romances that he decides to become a knight errant. Accompanied by his practical squire, Sancho Panza, he tilts at windmills and sees giants where others see ordinary life. Cervantes's sprawling comic masterpiece blends adventure, satire and reflection on illusion.

title: The Iliad
synopsis: In the tenth year of the Trojan War, the Greek warrior Achilles withdraws from battle after a bitter quarrel with the commander Agamemnon. Homer's epic poem follows the rage, honor and grief of heroes on both sides over a few weeks of fighting, focusing on the human cost of war.

title: Leaves of Grass
synopsis: Walt Whitman's sprawling collection celebrates the self, the body, democracy and ordinary Americans. Revised over several decades, its free verse catalogs the everyday and the cosmic with exuberant confidence, inviting readers to find themselves in its expansive, celebratory lines.

title: Dune
synopsis: Paul Atreides, heir to a noble family, is sent to the desert planet Arrakis, the only source of the galaxy's most valuable substance. As political intrigue and a struggle over the desert's ecology unfold, Frank Herbert's epic explores religion, power and the consequences of charismatic leadership.

title: The Left Hand of Darkness
synopsis: Genly Ai, an envoy from a galactic alliance, travels to the icy planet Gethen, where people have no fixed gender and shift cyclically. Ursula K. Le Guin's thoughtful novel uses a diplomatic mission to explore politics, trust and identity, and the difficulty of understanding a world that differs radically from one's own.

title: A Wizard of Earthsea
synopsis: On a remote archipelago where magic is taught as a discipline, a gifted but proud boy named Ged accidentally unleashes a dark shadow into the world. Ursula K. Le Guin's first Earthsea novel follows his education at a school of wizardry and his journey to face the consequences of his own pride.

title: Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep?
synopsis: In a ruined, post-apocalyptic San Francisco, bounty hunter Rick Deckard is assigned to retire rogue androids that have fled to Earth. Philip K. Dick's novel asks what makes us human, probing empathy, animals and identity while a dying world decays around its characters.

title: The Handmaid's Tale
subjects: Canadian fiction (fictional works by one author)
synopsis: In the Republic of Gilead, a theocracy built on the ruins of the United States, women are assigned roles based on fertility. Offred, a handmaid, narrates her life in a repressive household and recalls the freedom she once had. Margaret Atwood's chilling novel examines control of women's bodies, resistance and memory.

title: Never Let Me Go
synopsis: Kathy H. recalls her childhood at Hailsham, a seemingly idyllic English boarding school, and the friends who shaped her youth. As the children grow up, they gradually learn the truth about their place in the world. Kazuo Ishiguro's quiet, unsettling novel explores memory, love and the acceptance of fate.

title: The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy
synopsis: Arthur Dent wakes to find his house about to be demolished for a road, and his friend Ford Prefect reveals that Earth itself is due for demolition to make way for an intergalactic highway. Douglas Adams's comic science fiction follows the pair through absurd space-travel mishaps, armed with a towel and a guidebook.

title: Good Omens
subtitle: The Nice and Accurate Prophecies of Agnes Nutter, Witch
synopsis: An angel and a demon who have grown fond of earthly life over six thousand years team up to stop the Apocalypse from proceeding as scheduled. Terry Pratchett and Neil Gaiman's comedy follows their unlikely partnership as they hunt for the misplaced Antichrist, a satirical romp about faith, free will and friendship.

title: The Hobbit
synopsis: Bilbo Baggins, a comfortable hobbit, is recruited by the wizard Gandalf and a company of dwarves to reclaim a treasure guarded by the dragon Smaug. Tolkien's enchanting prelude to The Lord of the Rings follows Bilbo through forests, mountains and caves, discovering courage and a mysterious ring along the way.

title: A Game of Thrones
synopsis: Noble families vie for control of the Iron Throne in the realm of Westeros as a long summer shows signs of ending. Political intrigue, betrayal and war draw in the Stark, Lannister and Targaryen houses. George R.R. Martin's first volume sets dark, morally complex stakes in a richly imagined world.

title: The Name of the Wind
synopsis: Kvothe, now a reclusive innkeeper, recounts his extraordinary life to a chronicler. From a traveling troupe to his brilliant and troubled years at the university, Patrick Rothfuss follows a gifted young man determined to master magic and learn the truth behind his legend.

title: Mistborn: The Final Empire
synopsis: In a world where ash falls from the sky and a dark lord has ruled for a thousand years, a street thief discovers she can draw extraordinary power from metals. Brandon Sanderson's fast-moving heist fantasy follows her as she joins a crew planning the nearly impossible: overthrowing an immortal emperor.

title: The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe
synopsis: Four siblings discover a magical wardrobe that leads to the snowy land of Narnia, which lies under the spell of a wicked White Witch. C.S. Lewis's beloved children's fantasy follows Lucy, Edmund, Susan and Peter as they join the lion Aslan in a struggle between good and evil.

title: Piranesi
synopsis: Piranesi lives in a vast labyrinth of marble halls and statues, where tides flood the lower levels. He keeps careful records of his days and meets only one other person, whose messages hint at a larger world. Susanna Clarke's enigmatic novel unfolds as a puzzle about memory, identity and the house itself.

title: Six of Crows
synopsis: A crew of outcasts in a city of dangerous politics is offered a lucrative heist with an almost impossible target: a fortified prison. Leigh Bardugo's fast-paced young adult fantasy follows six skilled misfits, each with secrets of their own, as they work together and test whether they can trust one another.

title: Ninth House
synopsis: Alex Stern, a hardened survivor with a troubled past, is admitted to Yale on a scholarship to monitor the occult societies that hide dark powers on campus. When a student disappears, she uncovers a web of secret rituals and the people who run them. Leigh Bardugo's adult fantasy mixes campus mystery with supernatural menace.

title: Hell Bent
synopsis: Leigh Bardugo returns to the occult underworld of New Haven introduced in Ninth House. Alex Stern and her uneasy allies face a fresh and dangerous chapter, as the secret societies of the city and their old rivalries begin to unravel. A tense, atmospheric fantasy of dark magic and difficult loyalties.

title: The Poppy War
synopsis: Rin, a clever orphan from a poor southern village, wins a place at a prestigious military academy and discovers a dangerous, dormant power. R.F. Kuang's brutal, historically inspired fantasy examines war, colonial violence and the terrible price of power, drawing on the history and mythology of China.

title: Babel
subtitle: Or the Necessity of Violence
synopsis: In 1830s Oxford, the orphan Robin Swift is taken from Canton to study at the Royal Institute of Translation, where silver-working magic powers the British Empire. R.F. Kuang's novel explores colonialism, language and loyalty through a young scholar torn between his mentors and his own sense of identity.

title: The House in the Cerulean Sea
synopsis: Linus Baker, a caseworker for the Department in Charge of Magical Youth, is sent to inspect a mysterious orphanage on a remote island. Its six children and their enigmatic guardian challenge every assumption he holds. TJ Klune's warm, funny novel is about kindness, bureaucracy and finding family.

title: Legends & Lattes
synopsis: Viv, a battle-weary orc warrior tired of violence, decides to open a coffee shop in a quiet town. Travis Baldree's cozy fantasy follows her as she builds a business from scratch, befriends the locals and learns to find peace in ordinary things.

title: A Court of Thorns and Roses
synopsis: Feyre, a young huntress supporting her family in a human village, kills a wolf in the forest and is pulled into the magical realm of the Fae. There she must navigate a dangerous court of immortal beings and a relationship she never expected. Sarah J. Maas's romantic fantasy blends danger, desire and political intrigue.

title: Fourth Wing
synopsis: Violet Sorrengail, a scholar forced by her commanding mother into a brutal military academy for dragon riders, must survive a grueling training regimen. Rebecca Yarros's romantic fantasy combines dragon-riding action, a deadly academy hierarchy and an intense slow-burn romance in a kingdom on the brink of war.

title: Iron Flame
synopsis: Violet Sorrengail continues her perilous journey at the Basgiath War College, where danger lurks everywhere and old secrets threaten the fragile alliances among the riders. Rebecca Yarros's sequel escalates the dragon-filled conflict and the central romance, delivering high stakes and emotional turns.

title: Circe
synopsis: Exiled to a remote island by the gods, the minor nymph Circe discovers she has a gift for witchcraft. Madeline Miller's retelling of Greek myth follows her across centuries, through her encounters with mortals and immortals, toward hard-won independence, exploring power, loneliness and motherhood.

title: The Song of Achilles
synopsis: Patroclus, an exiled young prince, forms a bond with the gifted Achilles, son of a king and a goddess, while both train under the wise centaur Chiron. Madeline Miller's retelling of the Trojan War is a tender, tragic romance that follows the two men from boyhood toward the battlefield.

title: Gone Girl
synopsis: On his fifth wedding anniversary, Nick Dunne reports his wife, Amy, missing from their Missouri home. As the police and media descend, the investigation exposes cracks in their marriage and a series of unsettling secrets. Gillian Flynn's sharp thriller plays with perception, deception and the stories people tell about each other.

title: The Girl Who Played with Fire
synopsis: Lisbeth Salander, the unconventional hacker, returns to find herself accused of a triple murder just as she is preparing to expose a trafficking ring. Journalist Mikael Blomkvist, meanwhile, is closing in on the same story. Stieg Larsson's fast, twisting crime thriller tightens the tension around them.

title: The Silence of the Lambs
synopsis: FBI trainee Clarice Starling is assigned to interview the imprisoned psychiatrist Hannibal Lecter, whose insights might help identify a serial killer nicknamed Buffalo Bill. Thomas Harris's chilling thriller follows Clarice's unsettling psychological duel with Lecter as she races against time to find a kidnapped woman.

title: The Talented Mr. Ripley
synopsis: Tom Ripley, a charming drifter, is sent to Italy to persuade a wealthy young man to return home to America. Once there, Tom is seduced by the luxury of his world and begins to assume his identity. Patricia Highsmith's psychological thriller is a study of envy, deception and moral ambiguity.

title: And Then There Were None
synopsis: Ten strangers are invited to a remote island mansion off the Devon coast, each concealing a past that links them to an unpunished crime. As the guests die one by one, following a chilling nursery rhyme, they realize one of them is hunting the rest. Agatha Christie's classic is a masterpiece of suspense.

title: The Thursday Murder Club
synopsis: Four residents of a quiet retirement village meet each week to investigate unsolved cold cases. When a local developer is found dead, the group finds itself at the center of a real murder investigation. Richard Osman's cheerful mystery blends wit, warmth and clever deduction with a surprisingly moving look at ageing.

title: The Hunger Games
synopsis: In a dystopian nation divided into districts, sixteen-year-old Katniss Everdeen volunteers to take her younger sister's place in a televised fight to the death. Suzanne Collins's gripping novel explores media spectacle, oppression and survival, as Katniss relies on wit and courage inside the arena.

title: The Haunting of Hill House
synopsis: Dr. John Montague gathers a small group to spend a summer at Hill House, a notorious mansion with a reputation for violence. Among the guests is Eleanor Vance, whose fragile emotional life leaves her increasingly vulnerable to the house. Shirley Jackson builds psychological dread from the uncertainty of what is real.

title: It
synopsis: Seven childhood friends in the small town of Derry, Maine, are haunted by a shape-shifting creature that preys on children. Decades later, they reunite to confront the evil they once fought and to remember what they had buried. Stephen King's sprawling horror novel moves between childhood and adulthood.

title: The Shining
synopsis: Jack Torrance takes a job as winter caretaker at the isolated Overlook Hotel in the Colorado mountains, hoping to finish a writing project. His young son has psychic gifts that the hotel seems eager to exploit, and deep snow traps the family inside. Stephen King's novel explores addiction, family and the hotel's violent past.

title: Holly
synopsis: Private investigator Holly Gibney returns in a case that begins with a missing person and quickly reveals something darker. Stephen King's crime novel blends methodical detective work with the uncanny, following Holly's stubborn investigation and the people who cross her path in a small American town.

title: Mexican Gothic
synopsis: In 1950s Mexico, Noemí Taboada is sent to a remote English-owned estate after a frantic letter from her cousin. The mansion's decaying grandeur and secretive household hide a dark family history. Silvia Moreno-Garcia's gothic horror draws on classic influences and on themes of colonialism and power.

title: The Exorcist
synopsis: When twelve-year-old Regan begins behaving in disturbing ways, her mother seeks medical help and eventually turns to two priests for an exorcism. William Peter Blatty's horror novel examines faith, science and the fragility of innocence as the possession escalates toward terrifying extremes.

title: Me Before You
synopsis: Louisa Clark, a chatty and unambitious young woman, takes a job as a caregiver for Will Traynor, a former adventurous executive left paralyzed after an accident. As the two form an unexpected bond, Louisa's world widens in ways she never imagined. Jojo Moyes's romance explores love, independence and difficult choices.

title: Outlander
subjects: Culloden, Battle of, Scotland, 1746 in fiction
synopsis: In 1945, combat nurse Claire Randall is transported through standing stones in the Scottish Highlands back to 1743. Torn between her husband in the twentieth century and a dangerous new life, she is drawn into clan conflict and a passionate relationship with a rugged Highland warrior. Diana Gabaldon's historical romance blends time travel and adventure.

title: Normal People
synopsis: Marianne and Connell, two students from County Sligo, Ireland, have a complicated relationship that shifts between intimacy and distance as they move through school and university. Sally Rooney's literary novel observes the subtle power dynamics, class differences and emotional honesty that shape their bond over several years.

title: Intermezzo
synopsis: Two brothers, Peter and Ivan, face the death of their father and the strain of their romantic relationships. Sally Rooney's novel follows their emotional lives across Ireland, exploring grief, desire and the difficult work of loving people honestly. A quiet, intricate study of intimacy and family.

title: The Time Traveler's Wife
synopsis: Henry DeTamble, a librarian, has a genetic disorder that sends him involuntarily through time, and his wife, Clare, has grown up with his sudden disappearances and returns. Audrey Niffenegger's novel follows their love story across decades as they negotiate the strange logistics of a marriage and the limits of control.

title: Happy Place
synopsis: Harriet and Wyn dated for years, then broke up, yet they still spend one week each year at a beloved cottage in Maine. When they decide to hide the breakup from their friends, the pretense becomes a complicated test of memory and honesty. Emily Henry's romance is funny and warm.

title: It Ends with Us
subjects: Fiction, Romance, Contemporary, Life change events
synopsis: Lily Bloom, a young woman from a small Maine town, opens a flower shop in Boston and begins a relationship with a charming neurosurgeon named Ryle Kincaid. Her past with a first love resurfaces, complicating everything. Colleen Hoover's bestselling romance takes on love, family trauma and painful choices.

title: Lessons in Chemistry
synopsis: In 1960s California, Elizabeth Zott is a brilliant research chemist whose career is derailed by sexism and an unexpected romance. Pushed into hosting a television cooking show, she turns her scientific approach into an unlikely hit with viewers. Bonnie Garmus's witty novel is a warm celebration of intelligence and defiance.

title: Demon Copperhead
synopsis: Damon Fields, born to a teenage mother in the Appalachian mountains of Virginia, grows up in poverty and navigates foster care, addiction and hard work. Barbara Kingsolver's retelling of a Dickens classic gives the story a sharp, modern American voice and confronts class, opioids and resilience.

title: Tomorrow, and Tomorrow, and Tomorrow
synopsis: Sam and Sadie, childhood friends reunited years later at a Harvard dormitory, form a creative partnership designing video games. Across decades their collaboration brings triumph and heartbreak, tested by love, ambition and loyalty. Gabrielle Zevin's novel explores creativity, friendship and the meaning of play.

title: The Book Thief
synopsis: In Nazi Germany, nine-year-old Liesel Meminger is sent to live with a foster family near Munich. She steals books and begins reading aloud during air raids, forging a bond with a Jewish man hidden in her home. Narrated by Death, Markus Zusak's novel is a moving story of words and courage.

title: The Covenant of Water
synopsis: In early twentieth-century Kerala, a girl is married at twelve to a man she barely knows, and her life becomes entangled with a mysterious condition that affects women in her community. Abraham Verghese's epic novel spans generations and touches on faith, medicine and love in a changing India.

title: Tom Lake
synopsis: During the pandemic, three grown daughters ask their mother, a former actress, to recount a summer she spent at a cherry orchard in Michigan. Ann Patchett's novel weaves memories of youth, theater and first love into the present-day life of a family. A tender meditation on memory, motherhood and what endures.

title: Prophet Song
synopsis: In a near-future Dublin under authoritarian rule, Eilish Stack watches her family come apart as her husband is drawn into a rising political movement and the state tightens its grip. Paul Lynch's novel follows a mother's desperate fight to protect her children in a society sliding into terror.

title: Orbital
synopsis: Six astronauts orbit the Earth aboard the International Space Station, watching sunrises and the fragile planet below as they reflect on their lives over the course of a single day. Samantha Harvey's quiet, lyrical novel is a meditation on home, mortality and the beauty of the world.

title: James
synopsis: Percival Everett retells the story of Huckleberry Finn from the perspective of Jim, the enslaved man who escapes down the Mississippi River with a young boy. This sharp, witty reimagining examines identity, language and freedom, and the brutal history of slavery in America.

title: Chain-Gang All-Stars
subjects: Ferro-Grumley Award for LGBTQ Fiction Finalist
synopsis: In a near-future America where prisons are run for profit and inmates compete in a deadly televised sport, Nana Kwame Adjei-Brenyah's novel examines violence, race and the price of spectacle. Its sharp satire follows characters who struggle to survive in a system built to exploit them.

title: Creation Lake
synopsis: Sandrine, a former operative now working undercover, infiltrates a rural community of environmental activists in France. As her cover slips and her loyalties are tested, Rachel Kushner's tense novel explores surveillance, ideology and the moral ambiguity of protest.

title: Yellowface
synopsis: June Hayward, a struggling novelist, is stunned when her more successful friend and rival dies, leaving an unfinished manuscript behind. June takes the book and presents it as her own, and it becomes a bestseller amid controversy about authorship and race. R.F. Kuang's sharp satire examines publishing and ambition.

title: The Ministry of Time
synopsis: A British government official in the near future is recruited into a secret program that brings historical figures forward to live in the present. Assigned to care for a visitor from the nineteenth century, she finds the arrangement ethically fraught and emotionally complicated. Kaliane Bradley's novel mixes science fiction, bureaucracy and romance.

title: Sea of Tranquility
synopsis: Emily St. John Mandel's novel moves through several centuries and worlds, following characters linked by a mysterious event and by the sense that time is a fragile shared thread. Its gentle, reflective story explores art, loss and the quiet connections that survive across distance.

title: The Kaiju Preservation Society
synopsis: Jamie Gray, a struggling food-delivery worker in New York, stumbles into a job at a secret organization that studies giant monsters. John Scalzi's breezy comic science fiction follows Jamie and her quirky colleagues as they track a dangerous interdimensional threat, with sharp dialogue and a playful tone.

title: Hello Beautiful
synopsis: The Padavano family of a small New York town is shaped by the close bond between two sisters, Julia and Cinda, and by the marriage of a charming man named William. Ann Napolitano's novel follows several decades of family life, loss and reconciliation, examining how siblings and spouses hold one another together.

title: Remarkably Bright Creatures
synopsis: Tova Sullivan, a widowed cleaner at a Pacific Northwest aquarium, has spent years mourning her son. When she begins to befriend a giant Pacific octopus, the animal helps her uncover a mystery connected to her past. Shelby Van Pelt's warm novel explores grief, companionship and unlikely friendship.

title: Pineapple Street
synopsis: Jenny Jackson's comic novel follows a close-knit, wealthy family in Brooklyn Heights as their privileged lives are tested by money, marriage and class anxieties. Sharp observation of sibling bonds and the fragile line between love and obligation drives the story forward.

title: Trust
synopsis: Hernan Diaz's novel is built from four interlinked texts, including a novel within a memoir, that circle the fortune of a Wall Street financier and his wife in early twentieth-century New York. The book explores money, storytelling and the many competing versions of a single life.

title: The Seven Moons of Maali Almeida
synopsis: A war photographer wakes up dead in a lush afterlife in Sri Lanka, with seven moons in which to solve his own murder and guide his hidden photographs to the living. Shehan Karunatilaka's darkly comic Booker Prize-winning novel mixes satire, ghost story and a critique of a country scarred by civil war.

title: The Women
synopsis: During the Vietnam War, twenty-year-old nursing student Frances McGrath enlists and is sent to a military hospital, where she faces the hardships and horrors of war. Kristin Hannah's novel follows her experiences and the courage of the women who served, many of them overlooked by history.

title: The Nightingale
synopsis: In 1940s France, two sisters, Vianne and Isabelle, find their lives transformed when German troops occupy their village. One sister stays to protect her family while the other joins the Resistance. Kristin Hannah's novel explores courage, sacrifice and the bond between sisters in wartime.

title: All the Light We Cannot See
synopsis: A blind French girl and a German boy whose talent for radios draws him toward dangerous work both find their lives shaped by World War II. Anthony Doerr's novel alternates between occupied France and wartime Germany, exploring curiosity, memory and the quiet ways ordinary people resist.

title: Shogun
synopsis: The English navigator John Blackthorne is shipwrecked in feudal Japan in 1600, where he is drawn into the power struggles among rival warlords. James Clavell's sweeping epic follows his adaptation to an alien culture, his entanglement with political intrigue and his relationships with the people who shape his new life.

title: A Confederacy of Dunces
synopsis: Ignatius J. Reilly, an eccentric and self-important New Orleans man, is forced to find work after a mishap with his mother's car. His misadventures through jobs, schemes and romances make up a comic portrait of the city and its colorful, dysfunctional people. John Kennedy Toole's novel is a farce.

title: The Hate U Give
synopsis: Starr Carter, a sixteen-year-old from a poor neighborhood who attends a wealthy private school, witnesses the police shooting of her childhood friend. Caught between two worlds, she must decide whether to speak out. Angie Thomas's young adult novel explores race, activism and the courage to tell the truth.

title: The Giver
synopsis: In a seemingly perfect community with no pain, color or choice, twelve-year-old Jonas is chosen to become the Receiver of Memory. As he begins to learn the history the community has forgotten, he starts to see the cost of its safety. Lois Lowry's dystopian novel asks what makes life worth living.

title: The Outsiders
synopsis: Ponyboy Curtis, a teenager from the poorer side of town, is caught in a fierce rivalry between the Greasers and the wealthy Socs. A violent confrontation forces him to flee and face difficult choices about loyalty and class. S.E. Hinton's classic novel was written by a teenager and speaks to young readers.

title: The Fault in Our Stars
synopsis: Hazel, a sixteen-year-old living with terminal cancer, meets Augustus at a support group, and the two begin a romance through their shared love of books. John Green's young adult novel is funny, sharp and emotionally honest about illness, mortality and the meaning of a life that is short but full.

title: Ready Player One
subjects: YOUNG ADULT FICTION / Computers & Digital Media
YOUNG ADULT FICTION / Mysteries & Detective Stories
synopsis: In 2045, a dystopian world is escaped through OASIS, a vast virtual reality where people spend most of their lives. When its creator dies and leaves a hidden challenge behind, a teenager named Wade Watts joins a global hunt for an Easter egg. Ernest Cline's novel is a fast tribute to 1980s pop culture.

title: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone
synopsis: On his eleventh birthday, orphaned Harry Potter learns that he is a wizard and is whisked away to Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry. Befriending Ron and Hermione, he uncovers a dark secret about a stone that grants immortality. J.K. Rowling's enchanting first novel launched a global phenomenon.

title: The Lightning Thief
synopsis: Percy Jackson discovers that he is the son of a Greek god and is accused of stealing Zeus's lightning bolt. Forced to journey across America with two friends, he must face mythological monsters and uncover the truth before a war among the gods erupts. Rick Riordan's funny, fast-paced adventure brings myth to modern readers.

title: A Wrinkle in Time
synopsis: Meg Murry and her brilliant younger brother Charles Wallace travel through space and time with a mysterious neighbor to rescue their scientist father, who has been trapped by a dark power. Madeleine L'Engle's classic blends science fiction, fantasy and reflections on faith, love and courage.

title: Anne of Green Gables
synopsis: When an elderly brother and sister who wanted a boy to help on their Prince Edward Island farm receive an orphaned girl named Anne instead, a lively and imaginative friendship begins. L.M. Montgomery's classic follows Anne's adventures, mishaps and dreams at school and in her new home.

title: The Jungle Book
subjects: Romans, nouvelles, etc. pour la jeunesse
synopsis: Mowgli, a boy raised by wolves in the Indian jungle, is threatened by the tiger Shere Khan and must learn the laws of the jungle from his animal family. Rudyard Kipling's collection of stories blends adventure, animal fables and vivid tales of the jungle's creatures.

title: Black Beauty
synopsis: Told from the viewpoint of a horse, Black Beauty recounts his life from a happy colthood on a country estate through a series of owners, some kind and some cruel. Anna Sewell's classic novel was written to encourage kindness and better treatment of working horses.

title: Little House on the Prairie
publisher: Ying wen han sheng chu ban gong si
synopsis: The Ingalls family travels west by covered wagon to build a new home on the American frontier. Laura Ingalls Wilder recounts their hardships and triumphs, from building a log cabin to surviving a harsh winter, through the eyes of a young girl. A warm memoir-inspired story of pioneer life.

title: Charlotte's Web
synopsis: Wilbur, a small pig on a Maine farm, is saved from slaughter by a clever spider named Charlotte, who weaves messages into her web to persuade the farmers he is special. E.B. White's gentle story about friendship, loyalty and the cycle of life has charmed generations of young readers.

title: Where the Wild Things Are
subtitle: In the Night Kitchen,Outside Over There, Nutshell Library,Sign on Rosie's Door, Very Far Away
synopsis: Max, a boy sent to bed without supper for misbehaving, sails away to an island full of huge, unruly monsters. Maurice Sendak's picture book is a bold, imaginative story about anger, adventure and the comfort of coming home to love.

title: The Very Hungry Caterpillar
synopsis: A tiny caterpillar hatches on a Sunday morning and eats his way through a week of foods before building a cocoon and emerging as a beautiful butterfly. Eric Carle's bright, tactile picture book introduces days, counting and the wonder of transformation.

title: Goodnight Moon
synopsis: A young rabbit says goodnight to everything in a cozy green room, from the moon and the stars to the quiet old lady whispering hush. Margaret Wise Brown's bedtime classic uses gentle rhythm and soft, calming images to ease children into sleep.

title: Green Eggs and Ham
subjects: I Can Read It All By Myself
synopsis: A persistent, rhyming creature keeps pressing a reluctant young fellow to try a dish he says he will never eat, in a house, with a mouse, and on a boat. Dr. Seuss's classic picture book uses a small set of words to teach young readers about open-mindedness and trying new things.

title: The Cat in the Hat
synopsis: On a rainy afternoon, two children are left alone at home when a tall, mischievous cat arrives and turns the house upside down. Dr. Seuss's classic early reader uses simple rhyming text and playful chaos to teach children to read with confidence and delight.

title: Matilda
subjects: Romans, nouvelles, etc. pour la jeunesse
synopsis: Matilda is a precocious, bookish girl with neglectful parents and a cruel headmistress named Miss Trunchbull. Her extraordinary mind reveals itself in unexpected ways, and she begins to fight back against injustice. Roald Dahl's comic children's novel celebrates intelligence, kindness and courage.

title: Charlie and the Chocolate Factory
subjects: Children's Middle Grade Action & Adventure Books
synopsis: Charlie Bucket, a poor boy who lives with his family in a tiny house, wins one of five golden tickets to tour the mysterious chocolate factory of the eccentric Willy Wonka. Roald Dahl's whimsical story follows the tour's strange and sometimes frightening surprises, with a moral twist.

title: Smile
synopsis: After a fall at school damages her front teeth, young Raina endures a long and painful series of dental surgeries and braces. Raina Telgemeier's graphic memoir is a warm, funny and honest story about friendship, self-image and the awkward years of growing up.

title: Maus
synopsis: Art Spiegelman interviews his father, a Polish Jew who survived Auschwitz, and turns his memories into a graphic novel. Jews are drawn as mice and Nazis as cats in this powerful work about the Holocaust, memory and the difficult relationship between a father and son.

title: Persepolis
synopsis: Marjane Satrapi grows up in Tehran during the Islamic Revolution and the war with Iraq, and her memoir in black-and-white comic panels follows her childhood, adolescence and time abroad. A sharp, honest portrait of a young woman's coming of age amid political upheaval.

title: Watchmen
synopsis: In an alternate 1985, costumed heroes have been outlawed, and one of them is murdered. A retired vigilante begins investigating, and the case uncovers a conspiracy that threatens the world. Alan Moore's landmark graphic novel explores power, morality and the nature of heroism.

title: The Sandman
synopsis: When a dark magician captures Dream, the ruler of the realm of dreams, the Sandman embarks on a long and strange journey to reclaim his power. Neil Gaiman's sprawling graphic series blends myth, horror and literary references into a richly imagined mythology of stories.

title: Saga
subtitle: Volume One
synopsis: Two soldiers from opposite sides of a galactic war fall in love and have a child, a new life that threatens to upend the conflict around them. Brian K. Vaughan and Fiona Staples's graphic series is an epic, irreverent space opera about family, war and the costs of loyalty.

title: Fun Home
synopsis: Alison Bechdel grows up in a small Pennsylvania town where her father runs a funeral home and conceals his private life. Her graphic memoir traces their complicated relationship through childhood memories, literary references and the revelations that come as she comes of age.

title: Nimona
synopsis: Nimona, a shape-shifting teenager with a mischievous streak, becomes the sidekick of a disgraced villain who once aspired to be a hero. N.D. Stevenson's graphic novel is a funny, inventive story about friendship, loyalty and the blurry line between good and evil.

title: Ghost World
synopsis: Two sardonic teenage friends, Enid and Rebecca, drift through the suburbs of an American town after high school, mocking everything around them. Daniel Clowes's graphic novel is a sharp, bittersweet portrait of boredom, alienation and the painful changes that come with growing up.

title: The Arrival
synopsis: A man leaves his family to build a new life in a strange city where the people speak an unknown language and the customs are unfamiliar. Shaun Tan's wordless graphic novel uses surreal, detailed illustrations to capture the experience of migration, wonder and the search for belonging.

title: Akira
subjects: Comics & graphic novels, manga, science fiction
synopsis: In a rebuilt Neo-Tokyo after a devastating explosion, a motorcycle gang member develops frightening psychic powers. Katsuhiro Otomo's landmark manga is an epic cyberpunk story about government control, youthful rebellion and a dangerous new force.

title: The Complete Calvin and Hobbes
synopsis: Calvin, a mischievous six-year-old, and his stuffed tiger, Hobbes, who comes to life in Calvin's imagination, explore the world through adventures, schemes and philosophical musings. Bill Watterson's beloved comic strip is a gentle, funny study of childhood imagination.

title: Milk and Honey
synopsis: Rupi Kaur's short poems and illustrations are arranged in chapters on pain, love, loss and healing. Written in spare, direct language, the collection speaks to readers about heartbreak, self-worth and the quiet process of becoming whole.

title: Ariel
synopsis: Sylvia Plath's collection of poems, drawn from the final months of her life, is charged with intense imagery of rebirth, anger and the body. Its spare, vivid verses have become one of the most influential works of confessional poetry in the twentieth century.

title: The Hill We Climb
synopsis: Amanda Gorman's poem was written for and recited at the 2021 presidential inauguration. Its lines reflect on the nation's divisions, the hope of renewal and the shared work of building a more perfect union, looking toward a future of unity and courage.

title: Night Sky with Exit Wounds
synopsis: Ocean Vuong's debut collection of poems explores war, migration, queer desire and the aftermath of violence within a Vietnamese American family. Its lush, intimate lines move between memory and the body, finding beauty in the wreckage of history.

title: Devotions
synopsis: Mary Oliver's selected poems draw on a lifetime of attention to the natural world, from birds and seasons to the small creatures of ponds and fields. Her clear, luminous lines ask readers to notice, to pay attention and to find meaning in ordinary days.

title: Twenty Love Poems and a Song of Despair
synopsis: Pablo Neruda's early collection moves between tender love poems and darker songs of loneliness and loss. Written in a vivid and sensual voice, the poems celebrate desire, the natural world and the intensity of a passionate romance.

title: The Essential Rumi
synopsis: A selection of poems by the thirteenth-century Persian poet Rumi, translated into English. The mystical verses explore longing, love and the search for the divine, drawing images from everyday life, nature and the spiritual journey within each reader.

title: The Complete Poems of Emily Dickinson
synopsis: Emily Dickinson's complete poems, mostly written in private during her lifetime, were published after her death. Her compact, unconventional verses explore death, nature, faith, the interior life and the mysteries of consciousness with striking originality.

title: I Know Why the Caged Bird Sings
synopsis: Maya Angelou's first autobiography recounts her childhood in the American South and the years that followed, marked by racism, trauma and a love of literature. Her memoir is a powerful account of finding her voice and a sense of self despite the cruelty of the world.

title: Meditations
synopsis: Marcus Aurelius, the Roman emperor, wrote these private notes to himself as a guide to living with virtue, self-discipline and acceptance. Reflecting on duty, mortality and the nature of the universe, the book remains one of the most widely read works of Stoic philosophy.

title: The Republic
synopsis: Plato's dialogue, narrated by Socrates, asks what justice is and whether the just life is the happiest. Through a long conversation about the ideal city, the education of rulers and the nature of the soul, it explores politics, knowledge and the good life.

title: Nicomachean Ethics
synopsis: Aristotle's lectures on ethics examine what makes a human life good, arguing that happiness comes through the cultivation of virtue and practical wisdom. Discussing friendship, pleasure, courage and justice, the work has shaped Western moral philosophy for more than two thousand years.

title: Tao Te Ching
synopsis: This short, ancient Chinese text, attributed to Laozi, offers brief verses on the Tao, the natural way of the universe. Its paradoxical, poetic reflections on humility, simplicity and balance have influenced philosophy, religion and art for many centuries.

title: The Art of War
synopsis: Sun Tzu's ancient Chinese treatise on military strategy explores planning, deception, terrain and the importance of knowing both oneself and one's opponent. Its concise chapters have influenced military leaders, business strategists and readers across centuries.

title: Sapiens
subtitle: A Brief History of Humankind
synopsis: Yuval Noah Harari surveys the history of our species, from the emergence of early humans to the present day. He explores how cognitive abilities, agriculture, empires and shared myths such as money and religion shaped human societies and our growing dominance of the planet.

title: Guns, Germs, and Steel
subtitle: The Fates of Human Societies
synopsis: Jared Diamond asks why some human societies developed far more advanced technologies and political systems than others. Drawing on geography, biology and history, he argues that environmental factors, such as the availability of domesticable plants and animals, shaped the divergent paths of civilizations.

title: A Brief History of Time
synopsis: Stephen Hawking offers an accessible tour of cosmology, from the Big Bang and black holes to the nature of time itself. Written for general readers, the book explains ideas about space, relativity and quantum theory with few equations, conveying the questions physicists pursue about the universe.

title: The Selfish Gene
synopsis: Richard Dawkins argues that evolution is best understood from the viewpoint of genes, which act as replicators that shape the behavior of organisms. Introducing ideas such as the gene's-eye view, he explores altruism, cooperation and the origins of culture through the lens of natural selection.

title: Cosmos
synopsis: Carl Sagan takes readers on a journey through the history of science and the universe, from ancient astronomers to modern space exploration. Combining eloquent prose with vivid explanations of planets, stars and the origins of life, the book celebrates scientific curiosity and humanity's place in the cosmos.

title: On the Origin of Species
synopsis: Charles Darwin presents his theory of evolution by natural selection, drawing on years of observation of plants, animals and fossils. Carefully building his argument through examples of variation, inheritance and competition, the book transformed biology and explained the diversity of life on Earth.

title: Silent Spring
synopsis: Rachel Carson documents how synthetic pesticides accumulate in ecosystems and harm birds, fish and people. Combining scientific research with lyrical nature writing, her book helped launch the modern environmental movement and challenged assurances about the safety of widely used chemicals.

title: The Immortal Life of Henrietta Lacks
synopsis: Rebecca Skloot tells the story of Henrietta Lacks, a Black tobacco farmer whose cancer cells were taken without her knowledge in 1951. Those cells became the HeLa cell line, essential to modern medicine. The book traces her family's struggle with the medical world and the ethics of research.

title: The Emperor of All Maladies
synopsis: Siddhartha Mukherjee chronicles the history of cancer, from ancient remedies to modern genetics. Blending science, patient stories and historical narrative, the book examines the discoveries, failures and debates behind treatments, offering a Pulitzer Prize-winning account of a disease that continues to shape human life.

title: The Structure of Scientific Revolutions
publisher: Fondo de Cultura Económica de España
synopsis: Thomas Kuhn argues that science does not progress in a steady, cumulative way but through revolutions, in which dominant paradigms are replaced when anomalies accumulate. The book examines how scientific communities define problems and standards, and it has deeply influenced the philosophy of science.

title: Why We Sleep
synopsis: Matthew Walker, a neuroscientist, explains what happens in the brain and body during sleep and why it matters for memory, learning, emotion, immunity and health. Drawing on research, he argues that chronic sleep loss has serious consequences and offers practical guidance for better rest.

title: Thinking, Fast and Slow
synopsis: Nobel laureate Daniel Kahneman describes two systems of thought, one fast and intuitive, the other slow and deliberate. Drawing on decades of research on cognitive biases and decision-making, he shows how these systems shape everyday judgments, economic choices and errors in life.

title: Man's Search for Meaning
synopsis: Viktor Frankl, a psychiatrist, recounts his experiences in Nazi concentration camps and the lessons he drew about finding purpose even in extreme suffering. The book introduces logotherapy, an approach centered on the human search for meaning as a fundamental motivation.

title: Influence
synopsis: Robert Cialdini identifies principles of persuasion, including reciprocity, commitment, social proof and scarcity, and explains how they operate in everyday life and in business. Drawing on years of field research and observation of sales professionals, he shows why people say yes.

title: The Power of Habit
synopsis: Charles Duhigg explains how habits form, how they can be changed and why they matter for individuals, organizations and societies. Using examples from business, medicine and civil rights, he presents a framework built on the habit loop of cue, routine and reward.

title: Mindset
synopsis: Psychologist Carol Dweck distinguishes between a fixed mindset, which sees abilities as unchangeable, and a growth mindset, which sees them as developed through effort and learning. Drawing on decades of research, she examines how these beliefs affect motivation, relationships, education and performance.

title: The Body Keeps the Score
subtitle: Brain, Mind, and Body in the Healing of Trauma
synopsis: Psychiatrist Bessel van der Kolk explores how trauma reshapes the brain, body and mind, and how survivors carry its effects long after the events have passed. Drawing on decades of clinical work, he discusses emerging treatments that help people reconnect with the present.

title: Stolen Focus
synopsis: Johann Hari investigates the causes of our collective loss of attention, looking at technology, work culture, stress and modern life. Drawing on interviews and research, he argues that focus is a social and environmental problem as well as a personal one, and he offers ideas for reclaiming concentration.

title: The Anxious Generation
synopsis: Jonathan Haidt argues that the rapid shift to smartphones and social media in the early 2010s has contributed to a surge in anxiety, depression and self-harm among young people. He proposes norms, including no smartphones before high school, to help children regain independence, play and real-world connection.

title: Atomic Habits
synopsis: James Clear offers a practical framework for building good habits and breaking bad ones through small, incremental changes. Drawing on research in psychology and biology, he introduces ideas such as identity-based habits, habit stacking and environmental design as a system for lasting improvement.

title: How to Win Friends and Influence People
synopsis: Dale Carnegie's classic guide offers practical advice on building relationships, making people like you and persuading others without conflict. Organized into principles illustrated with anecdotes, the book emphasizes appreciation, genuine interest in others and the art of listening.

title: The 7 Habits of Highly Effective People
synopsis: Stephen Covey presents seven principles for personal and professional effectiveness, moving from dependence to independence to interdependence. The book emphasizes character, proactive thinking, prioritizing important goals and renewing oneself, and it has become one of the most widely read self-improvement books.

title: The Subtle Art of Not Giving a F*ck
synopsis: Mark Manson argues that a satisfying life comes not from positive thinking but from choosing which problems are worth caring about. With blunt humor and personal anecdotes, he explores values, responsibility and accepting limits, offering a counterpoint to the self-help genre's obsession with constant optimism.

title: The Let Them Theory
synopsis: Mel Robbins presents a simple idea: let other people think, feel and act the way they want, and stop trying to control what you cannot change. Blending personal stories with practical exercises, the book aims to help readers reduce stress, set boundaries and focus on their own choices.

title: Deep Work
subtitle: Rules for Focused Success in a Distracted World
synopsis: Cal Newport argues that the ability to focus without distraction on demanding tasks is increasingly valuable and rare. He describes strategies for building deep work habits, from scheduling and rituals to limiting shallow activity, and makes the case that this skill drives professional success and satisfaction.

title: Range
subtitle: Why Generalists Triumph in a Specialized World
synopsis: David Epstein contends that generalists, who explore widely and sample many different fields, often outperform specialists in complex and unpredictable domains. Drawing on research in sports, science and the arts, he explores the value of breadth and delayed specialization in building adaptable careers.

title: Ikigai
subtitle: The Japanese Secret to a Long and Happy Life
synopsis: Héctor García and Francesc Miralles explore the Japanese concept of ikigai, a sense of purpose or reason for living, through stories of people in Okinawa, a region known for longevity. The book reflects on health, friendship, routine and mindfulness as ways to find meaning in everyday life.

title: The Creative Act
subtitle: A Way of Being
synopsis: Music producer Rick Rubin shares reflections on creativity, drawn from decades of working with artists across genres. Rather than offering a formula, the book explores attention, intuition, listening and the discipline of living in a way that makes creative work possible.

title: Good to Great
synopsis: Jim Collins and his research team identify companies that moved from good results to sustained excellence and compare them with rivals that did not. The book distills the common traits of leadership, discipline, culture and strategy that separated these long-term winners from the rest.

title: Zero to One
subtitle: Notes on Startups, or How to Build the Future
subjects: POLITICAL SCIENCE / Public Policy / Economic Policy
synopsis: Peter Thiel argues that the greatest businesses create something genuinely new rather than copying existing models. Drawing on his experience as an entrepreneur and investor, he discusses monopoly, technology, timing and the founder's mindset as keys to building the future.

title: The Hard Thing About Hard Things
synopsis: Ben Horowitz shares lessons from leading a software company through brutal periods of crisis, layoffs and competition. Candid and practical, the book addresses the emotional difficulty of leadership, hiring, firing and making hard decisions under pressure, offering advice for founders.

title: Lean In
subjects: Sex role in the work environment
synopsis: Sheryl Sandberg examines why women remain underrepresented in leadership and offers advice on ambition, mentorship and partnership at home and at work. Blending personal experience with research, she encourages women to pursue their goals and to challenge the internal and external barriers that hold them back.

title: Start with Why
synopsis: Simon Sinek argues that great leaders and organizations begin with their purpose, or why they do what they do, rather than focusing only on what they sell. Using examples from business and history, he explains how this idea inspires loyalty and builds lasting trust.

title: Shoe Dog
subtitle: A Memoir by the Creator of Nike
synopsis: Phil Knight, co-founder of Nike, recounts the early years of building the company from a small import business into a global brand. Written with candor and humor, the memoir describes the struggles, risks, personal sacrifices and relationships that shaped Nike's rise.

title: Steve Jobs
subtitle: Lecciones de liderazgo
synopsis: Walter Isaacson's biography draws on dozens of interviews with Apple's co-founder and with his family, friends and rivals. It portrays Jobs as a visionary, perfectionist and often difficult leader whose products transformed computing, music and mobile phones, and it examines his intense personality.

title: Freakonomics
synopsis: Steven Levitt and Stephen Dubner use economic reasoning to examine unexpected questions, from the link between crime and legalized abortion to how names and cheating reveal hidden incentives. The book shows how data analysis can uncover surprising truths about everyday behavior.

title: Bad Blood
synopsis: John Carreyrou investigates Theranos, the startup that promised revolutionary blood tests from a few drops of blood and attracted celebrated investors. Through interviews and documents, he reveals the company's deception, the pressures of Silicon Valley and the courage of employees who came forward.

title: Careless People
synopsis: Sarah Wynn-Williams, a former Facebook policy executive, recounts her years at the company and her experiences with its leadership, decisions and internal culture. The memoir describes the pressures of rapid growth, the company's relations with governments and the personal costs of working inside a powerful firm.

title: Empire of AI
subtitle: Dreams and Nightmares in Sam Altman’s OpenAI
publisher: Penguin Random House Audio Publishing Group
synopsis: Karen Hao, a journalist who has covered artificial intelligence for years, examines the rise of leading AI companies and the race to build ever-larger models. She investigates their ambitions, their culture, their environmental and labor impacts, and the concentration of power the technology brings.

title: Fire Weather
synopsis: John Vaillant tells the story of the 2016 Fort McMurray wildfire in Alberta, Canada, which grew into a firestorm that destroyed much of the town. Blending reporting, science and history, the book examines how climate change and extreme weather combine to create catastrophic fires.

title: Team of Rivals
synopsis: Doris Kearns Goodwin examines how Abraham Lincoln assembled a cabinet of former political rivals, several of whom had sought the presidency themselves. Drawing on extensive research, she explores Lincoln's leadership, humility and political skill during the Civil War and a period of bitter division.

David McCullough recounts the year that began the American Revolution, focusing on George Washington and the Continental Army. Through vivid narrative and firsthand accounts, the book follows the battles, retreats and hardships of an army that struggled to survive and keep the cause of independence alive.

title: John Adams
synopsis: David McCullough's biography follows John Adams, the second president and a principled, combative founder. Drawing on letters and diaries, the book explores his role in the Revolution, his diplomacy abroad, his partnership with his wife, Abigail, and his complicated legacy in the young republic.

title: The Devil in the White City
synopsis: Erik Larson weaves two stories around the 1893 Chicago World's Fair: the ambitious architects building its dazzling White City, and a murderer who used the fair to lure victims. The narrative explores urban ambition, architecture and the darker side of progress.

title: Between the World and Me
synopsis: Ta-Nehisi Coates writes a letter to his teenage son about growing up Black in America, the fear and danger he experienced, and the historical forces that shape Black lives. The book reflects on race, the body and what freedom really means.

title: The Autobiography of Malcolm X
synopsis: Written with Alex Haley, this autobiography traces the life of Malcolm X from a childhood marked by loss to his transformation through prison, the Nation of Islam and a pilgrimage to Mecca. It is a powerful record of racial injustice, self-invention and the struggle for human rights.

title: A People's History of the United States
subtitle: 1492-present
synopsis: Howard Zinn retells American history from the perspective of workers, enslaved people, women, immigrants and Native Americans rather than presidents and generals. Covering events from Columbus to the late twentieth century, the book challenges traditional narratives and centers social struggle.

title: SPQR
synopsis: Mary Beard tells the story of ancient Rome, from its legendary founding to the late empire, emphasizing the lives of ordinary people as well as emperors and generals. Drawing on archaeology and classical sources, she examines how Rome built its power, politics and myths.

title: Educated
subtitle: A Memoir
synopsis: Tara Westover grows up in a survivalist family in rural Idaho, never attending school, and eventually makes her way to Cambridge University and a doctorate. Her memoir recounts the family conflicts and the self-invention that shaped her journey toward education and self-knowledge.

title: Becoming
synopsis: Michelle Obama recounts her life, from her childhood on Chicago's South Side through her years as a lawyer, her marriage and her time as First Lady. Reflecting on identity, family, ambition and resilience, the memoir offers an intimate account of finding one's own voice.

title: Born a Crime
synopsis: Trevor Noah recalls growing up in South Africa under apartheid as the son of a Black mother and a white Swiss father, a relationship that was illegal at the time. Told through funny and poignant stories, the memoir explores family, faith and identity, and how his mother's determination shaped him.

title: Yes Please
synopsis: Amy Poehler shares stories from her career in comedy, from improv beginnings to Saturday Night Live and television work. Mixing humor with candid advice, the book reflects on confidence, friendship, parenting and the value of saying yes to opportunities.

title: Bossypants
synopsis: Tina Fey recounts her path from a Pennsylvania childhood through improv, Saturday Night Live and writing for television. Her funny, self-deprecating memoir offers observations on working in comedy as a woman, balancing career and family, and the everyday experiences that shaped her outlook.

title: Wild
subjects: Pacific (AK, CA, HI, NV, OR, WA)
synopsis: After a series of personal losses, Cheryl Strayed sets out to hike more than a thousand miles of the Pacific Crest Trail alone, despite having little experience. Her memoir recounts the physical hardships, emotional reckoning and self-discovery of a solo journey through the wilderness.

title: Eat, Pray, Love
subtitle: One Woman's Search for Everything Across Italy, India and Indonesia
synopsis: Elizabeth Gilbert, newly divorced and unsettled, travels to Italy, India and Indonesia in search of pleasure, spiritual insight and balance. Her memoir mixes travel writing with reflection on faith, appetite and self-acceptance, and it resonated with many readers seeking a fresh start.

title: Into the Wild
synopsis: Jon Krakauer tells the story of Chris McCandless, a young graduate who gave away his savings and set out across America before attempting to survive alone in the Alaskan wilderness. Combining reporting with the author's own climbing experience, the book explores idealism, risk and the pull of the wild.

title: Into Thin Air
subtitle: A Personal Account of the Mt. Everest Disaster
synopsis: Jon Krakauer, a journalist on a 1996 Everest expedition, describes a disastrous climbing season that killed several members of the guided teams. Writing from his own perspective and that of other climbers, he examines commercial mountaineering, decision-making in extreme conditions and the limits of endurance.

title: In Cold Blood
synopsis: Truman Capote's nonfiction novel recounts the 1959 murder of a Kansas farming family by two drifters. Following the investigation, the trial and the killers' final days, the book blends reporting with novelistic technique to explore violence, justice and the roots of crime.

title: Helter Skelter
subtitle: The True Story of the Manson Murders
synopsis: Prosecutor Vincent Bugliosi recounts the investigation and trial of Charles Manson and his followers for the 1969 murders in Los Angeles. Drawing on case files and courtroom evidence, he details the crimes and the motives behind them, offering one of the most influential accounts of the era.

title: Killers of the Flower Moon
subtitle: The Osage Murders and the Birth of the FBI
subjects: United States. Federal Bureau of Investigation
United states, federal bureau of investigation
synopsis: David Grann investigates a series of murders of wealthy Osage people in 1920s Oklahoma, crimes tied to a scheme to seize their oil-rich land. The book follows the emerging FBI and its early investigation, revealing a long-hidden chapter of greed, corruption and racial violence in America.

title: Under the Banner of Heaven
subtitle: A Story of Violent Faith
synopsis: Jon Krakauer investigates the 1984 murders of a young woman and her infant daughter in Utah, crimes committed by two brothers who claimed divine inspiration. The book probes the history of fundamentalist Mormonism and the relationship between religious faith, obedience and violence.

title: The Psychopath Test
synopsis: Jon Ronson, a journalist, sets out to understand psychopathy after a book on the subject leads him to encounters with criminals, psychiatrists and self-proclaimed experts. Blending humor and curiosity, he questions how labels are applied to people and what it means to judge someone as evil.

title: The Stranger Beside Me
synopsis: Ann Rule, a crime writer who once worked alongside Ted Bundy at a crisis hotline, recounts his crimes and her personal connection to him. Combining true crime reporting with memoir, the book examines how a charming man concealed monstrous acts and how the investigation unfolded.

title: A Walk in the Woods
synopsis: Bill Bryson decides to hike the Appalachian Trail with a reluctant old friend, and through setbacks and encounters with wildlife and small-town America, he documents the quirks of the landscape. His humorous travelogue combines natural history, self-deprecation and sharp observation.

title: In a Sunburned Country
synopsis: Bill Bryson returns to Australia to explore its vast landscape, unusual wildlife and dangerous environment. With wit and curiosity, he recounts the country's history, eccentric characters and surprising natural wonders, from deserts and coastal cities to the outback's strange creatures.

title: Three Men in a Boat
synopsis: Three friends and a dog take a leisurely boat trip up the Thames from London, and their misadventures supply the comic material of this Victorian classic. Jerome K. Jerome's narrator delivers digressions, fishing mishaps and tangled chores with affectionate, self-deprecating humor.

title: Under the Tuscan Sun
subtitle: at home in Italy
synopsis: After a painful divorce, Frances Mayes buys a dilapidated villa in the Tuscan countryside and begins restoring it. Her memoir describes the renovation, the local food and culture, and the friendships she forms, celebrating the pleasures of rebuilding a life in a new place.
